decision: Reject and revert the scalar memo prototype; keep the production direct reader unchanged.
reproduce: Apply the experiment patch to runtime 384c4f5 and run pnpm exec tsc -b.
Run node bench/top-k-reader-comparison.mjs for shapes; set LAKEQL_KEY_CACHE_MATRIX=cardinality for cardinality/pressure.
Baseline defaults to 384c4f5; report records source/module hashes and distinguishes shared dependencies from a whole-revision comparison.
prototype: Initially tried two scalar slots, then reduced to a single retained right operand to reduce bookkeeping.
Enabled reuse only for steady candidate probing, keeping detection/heap construction/final sorting direct.
Admitted optional metadata; released it when required scalar growth needed its capacity.
Declined optional reuse inside fixed admitted stages, whose released reservations do not replenish stage allowance.

validation.cleanup: All successful/failed benchmark trials ended with zero reservations.
validation.correctness: Every result matched the independent stable row-sort oracle.

reason: The prototype wins all 32 nulls-last shape cases but loses 27 of 32 nulls-first cases.
Scope/optional-metadata bookkeeping adds complexity without a broadly reliable improvement.
Null-heavy comparisons warrant direct inspection before adding cache-policy heuristics; no new configuration knob is justified by this evidence.
boundaries: Prototype tests cover repeated decode counts, exact-cap growth with sibling isolation, fixed-stage fallback, vector identity, consumer failure and mutable reads with reuse disabled.
This is local synchronous Node kernel evidence, not cloud or whole-runtime memory proof.
Production runtime and its last complete regular/Worker checks remain unchanged after reverting the experiment.
Broader F5/M1/M2 integration and final release acceptance remain open.
